summary: Duplicate prorated stub credit applied after Dedicated capacity resumed from paused state
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a prorated "stub" reserved-credit applied twice to their account after their Dedicated capacity was resumed from a paused state during our maintenance window. The duplicate credit shows as two separate line items for the same hour and same reserved pool.

Impact:
- Customer LumenQ Labs saw an unexpected credit of $240 applied twice (total $480) against March reserved hours, causing invoice line variance and an accounting mismatch between their internal ledger and our invoice. They are unsure whether to accept the adjustment or request a reversal.
- No application-facing downtime was reported; this is a metering/billing discrepancy only.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster for LumenQ Labs (dedicated-reserve-87)
- Region: us-east-1
- Resume event timestamp: 2026-03-09T22:03:12Z (during scheduled maintenance window)
- Billing system: hourly postback reconciler + proration service (prod)

Steps to reproduce (customer observed):
1) Resume dedicated capacity after scheduled pause.
2) Run normal workload; system reported reserved-hour consumption for hour window 22:00-23:00.
3) Billing shows two prorated credit line-items with identical metadata (same meter tag, same hour) posted ~1m apart.

Expected behavior:
- One prorated credit (stub credit) should be applied for the paused-to-resume hour to adjust reserved-hour charges.

Actual behavior:
- Two stub credits were created for the same hour and same reserved pool. The credits were separate line items and both reduced the customer's invoice.

Logs / Artifacts:
- Billing event IDs: bill_evt_20260309_2230_01, bill_evt_20260309_2230_02
- Postback reconciler logs: s3://redwood-logs/prod/postback-reconciler/2026/03/09/22/*.log
- Customer supplied screenshot of invoice lines (attached to ticket).

investigation_notes: Initial log review showed two postback events for the same reserved-hour window. Reconciler delivered both because the deduplication key was hour+pool. During resume from paused state, a transient timeout during the first postback caused a retry with a new event UUID; because dedup key didn't include the event UUID or the reconciler request id, the retry was treated as distinct. Reproducer: artificial injection of a 500ms TCP delay to postback endpoint during resume triggers duplicate postback with identical hour metadata. Charging math validated: single stub credit should equal 240.00 USD; duplicate caused 480.00 USD credit. Root cause: deduplication key too coarse + race with resume flow that briefly emits identical metadata twice while exchanging state between scheduler and postback worker. Related PR fixes dedup to use (event_uuid || request_id) + hour + pool and adds idempotency token for resumptions. See GH PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-service/pull/448 and incident notes in INT-2201.
resolution: Workaround applied: created compensating reversal entry for the duplicate credit on 2026-03-13 15:10Z. Accounting will generate a credit memo documenting the reversal; invoice will be adjusted and a note added to the customer's billing dashboard. Permanent fix: merged PR #448 which tightens deduplication keys and adds idempotency tokens in the postback flow. Deploy plan: staged to staging on 2026-03-13, rolling prod deploy scheduled for 2026-03-17 during maintenance window with smoke tests for dedicated resume flows. Postmortem owner: Priya Rao (Postback team). Follow-ups: add alert on duplicate stub credits >1 per-hour per-pool and run a retroactive audit for last 30 days to ensure no other customers affected. Customer communication: emailed LumenQ Labs 2026-03-13 with explanation and expected timeline; accounting will follow with formal credit memo.
